title: Writing and rehearsals in the Oliver band
summary: Dave Nelson wrote the arrangements; the band rehearsed at Lafayette Hall twice a week for a month; Oliver used three trumpets.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Freddie, I really wanted to ask you a few questions about the King Oliver period. I was mostly interested in who did the writing, who did some of the writing for the band. Who wrote the arrangements for King Oliver? Or did he write them himself?
No, Dave Nelson.
Dave Nelson wrote the arrangements.
Yeah. A trumpet player, who was King Oliver's niece (sic).
Nephew.
Yes.

All right. And you mentioned a little bit about rehearsals that Oliver used to have and that he, of course, began to add on more trumpet players as his lip facility began to undergo this change and began to deteriorate.
Yes.
So did he take part in the rehearsals as that was going on?
Yes, he did. On some numbers, he'd take part in rehearsals. But he had three trumpet players. He always used three trumpets.
Moore (III) - 2
Where did you rehearse? Where did the Alamo Band rehearse?
At the Lafayette Theatre.
At the theatre itself.
Not the Lafayette Theatre, but the Lafayette Hall upstairs, one flight up.
I see. And about what time of the day would these rehearsals take place?
They used to take place around... Always around two o'clock, two until four, about twice a week. That went on, oh, about a month; we rehearsed twice a week for a whole month.

Were there any numbers in particular that caused the band any difficulties, that say Dave Nelson would have everybody go through the charts over and over again? Were there any that were particularly difficult?
No, not too much. They had mostly... Well, Red Elkins, he was doing the... He was the second trumpet player.
You mentioned him earlier.

Maybe Red Allen. He didn't do very much rehearsing because he didn't have time for it. Sometimes he'd do a matinee at the Metropole. He started to work down there early. And he used Louis Metcalf on some of them.
Moore (III) - 3
King Oliver, you mean.
Yes. I think he had the pyorrhea in his teeth, mouth..
The gums.
The gums, yeah.
